newsitem.title: USA: Santa Fe, Newmont in confidentiality pact.
newsitem.headline: Santa Fe, Newmont in confidentiality pact.

text.p: Santa Fe Pacific Gold Corp Chairman Patrick James said Monday his company entered a confidentiality agreement with Newmont Mining Corp prior to Newmont's announcement last Thursday of an unwelcome bid to acquire Santa Fe.
He declined comment on the agreement's current status.
Santa Fe today announced a pact to merge with Homestake Mining Co under terms richer than the Newmont bid.
Typically, a confidentiality agreement gives a suitor access to non-public documents in order to construct a bid that adequately reflects a target's value.
Santa Fe shareholders will own 50 percent of the combined Santa Fe/Homestake company, James told Reuters in an interview.
Half of the $50 million in one-time costs from the deal will be related to transaction fees, and half will be from employee severance costs, he said.

The companies said earlier they will merge on a tax-free exchange of shares at a ratio of 1.115 Homestake shares for each Santa Fe share, worth $17.42 per Santa Fe share, or $2.3 billion, based on Homestake's closing stock price last Friday.
Newmont's bid, which was also a tax-free share exchange, valued Santa Fe at almost $15.50 per share, also based on Friday's close.
